chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'For everyone there is an enthusiasm (shirrah), and for every enthusiasm there is a decline (fitrah). So, 'Tuba' (a tree in Paradise) is for the one whose decline is towards goodness.'

key_terms.شِرَّةٌ: Enthusiasm, vigor, or peak energy period
key_terms.طُوبَى: Tuba, a tree in Paradise or a state of bliss
key_terms.فَتْرَةٌ: Decline, ease, or period of reduced intensity
key_terms.فَطُوبَى: So, happiness/blessedness (often used as an exclamatory promise of reward)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'shirrah' and 'fitrah' in the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the natural human cycle of spiritual intensity (shirrah) followed by a period of ease or decline (fitrah), emphasizing that the quality of this subsequent phase determines one's ultimate fate. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, highlights the Shia emphasis on self-awareness and the strategic use of post-enthusiasm periods for consolidation of faith rather than complacency. The promise of 'Tuba' (bliss) serves as a motivational anchor, encouraging believers to ensure their 'fitrah' leads to enduring righteousness.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘For everyone is an enthusiasm, and every enthusiasm has a decline. So ‘Tuba’ (a tree in the Paradise) is for the one whose nature was to goodness’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hajjal from Tha’labah who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Everyone has an enthusiasm and every enthusiasm has a decline. Tuba (a tree in paradise) is for those whose decline is toward a constructive side.’”
